teams.heading: Fiji slumped to a third consecutive defeat against Scotland in July
teams.body: Fiji endured a difficult summer series, culminating in a 17-33 home loss against Scotland in July's Nations Championship group stage. That result in their most recent game extended a disappointing run of form for the national side. Across their last five international fixtures, the team have managed only one win alongside four defeats. This current run of three straight losses leaves the squad searching for answers.

teams.heading: Jeremy Guscott urges Steve Borthwick to hand Henry Pollock a starting spot
teams.body: Former England centre Jeremy Guscott has called on Steve Borthwick to start rising star Henry Pollock, describing the 21-year-old loose forward as "one of the most gifted players we have ever seen as a seven." The Northampton Saints back-rower has won 13 caps but made only one start, against Ireland in the Six Nations, usually being deployed as an impact player off the bench. Guscott also questioned the omission of Max Ojomoh and urged Borthwick to let Lee Blackett exert more influence.

teams.heading: France beat Japan 42-15 to secure third place in tournament standings
teams.body: France are third in the 12-team standings after three matches of the tournament. They registered two victories and one defeat in that opening three-match window. Les Bleus scored 116 points across those three fixtures. They conceded 75 points over the same period, leaving them with a points difference of +41 after their 42-15 victory over Japan in the third round. Historically, the team's longest unbroken spell at No. 1 in the world rankings lasted for one week, a milestone reached in July 2022.

teams.heading: Jamie Ritchie signs for Glasgow Warriors following season with USA Perpignan
teams.body: Former Scotland captain Jamie Ritchie has completed a move to Glasgow Warriors after spending last season in France with Top 14 side USA Perpignan. The 29-year-old back-rower, who won 63 caps and previously made 133 appearances for Glasgow's rivals Edinburgh, joins Franco Smith’s side ahead of the new United Rugby Championship season. Ritchie’s arrival offsets significant summer departures for the Warriors, who have lost Scotland internationals Huw Jones, Adam Hastings and Jack Dempsey.

teams.heading: Alun Wyn Jones joins Ospreys board to fight Welsh regional axe
teams.body: Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones has joined the Ospreys board of directors with immediate effect. The 40-year-old, who made 257 appearances for the region before retiring in 2023, returns as a director during a turbulent period for domestic rugby. The Welsh Rugby Union plans to reduce professional sides from four to three by 2028, putting the Swansea-based region's future in jeopardy. Jones stated his move is about bringing together his playing and business experience to "help drive long-term growth and stability for the organisation."

teams.heading: Tomás Albornoz handed four-match ban for intimidating referee Angus Gardner
teams.body: Argentina fly-half Tomás Albornoz has been suspended for four matches after accepting a misconduct charge for intimidating referee Angus Gardner. The incident occurred following the controversial 31-24 defeat to England in Santiago del Estero, where the Pumas were denied a last-gasp try. Albornoz approached the Australian official twice and had to be restrained by teammates. His suspension ruled him out of the Test against South Africa, the double-header against Australia, and a French Top 14 fixture with Toulon.

teams.heading: Les Kiss extends playmaker search as Wallabies prepare for Argentina tour
teams.body: The Wallabies’ search for a settled playmaker pairing remains unresolved as head coach Les Kiss continues to experiment. Following Carter Gordon’s impressive return at fly-half in the 56-17 win over Japan on 15 August, Kiss has yet to lock in his first-choice combinations before the upcoming matches in Argentina. While reports hint at a potential return for veteran Quade Cooper, there is no official word from camp, leaving the crucial position open as Australia’s World Cup preparations intensify.

teams.heading: Japan suffered heavy defeat in Townsville after Les Kiss reshuffled Wallabies
teams.body: Following injury concerns, Australia head coach Les Kiss resolved his selection puzzle, explaining he "looked to find some balance" by making eight changes for the rematch on 15 August. The strategy paid off in Townsville, where the Wallabies ran in eight tries to condemn Japan to a heavy 56-17 defeat. Although university student Ryunosuke Ito sparked an early reply, Japan faded as Australia cruised clear.

teams.heading: Richie Mo'unga returns as Dave Rennie names new All Blacks side for Lions
teams.body: Richie Mo’unga will make his first appearance for the All Blacks since the 2023 World Cup final after being named at fly-half for Tuesday’s match against the Lions. Coach Dave Rennie has overhauled his starting XV following Saturday’s 33-16 victory over the Springboks, making 15 changes for the fixture at Ellis Park. Mo’unga has been playing in Japan and Rennie noted he “gets the chance to put a bit of pressure on” rival Ruben Love as New Zealand target a clean sweep of South African franchises.

lead.why: Richie Mo’unga’s return to the starting lineup after a three-year international absence is the most significant selection event of the current tour.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus names South Africa side early following New Zealand defeat
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has reverted to his traditional early-week team announcement following Saturday’s 33-16 loss to New Zealand at Ellis Park. The Springboks coach, who delayed his selection until Thursday for the series opener as a tactical precaution, will confirm his matchday 23 for the second Test in Cape Town today. Changes are expected after injuries to both wings disrupted the backline in Johannesburg, with Dave Rennie predicting the world champions will "double down" on their set-piece and aerial approach.
